_doc: Which models the company may run agents on. company/tools/hire.js refuses anything not listed under allowed (candidates, hires and model changes). routing says which model each routine runs on; company/tools/pacer.js applies it within the pacing rule (company/work/finance/pacing-policy.json). The people seat (co.seatFor('people')) keeps this file; the CEO approves changes. Human version: company/MODEL_POLICY.md.

deepseek.note: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash only: frontier quality at a low cost, pay-per-use and prepaid. The fallback when the subscriptions are closed to a routine; kept under the station's daily rail. deepseek-v4-pro is not on the list (more expensive for no gain on this work).

custom.note: MiniMax Coding Plan: a flat-fee subscription with a 5-hour window and a weekly limit, used as much as the pacing rule allows. preferred is the model to move to once the plan serves it on the company's key; until then the routing table uses the Flash model.

claude-cli.note: Runs on a Claude Max subscription (flat monthly fee). The meter is the whole account, so any other use of the same account (the owner's own Claude Code, another company) counts against it; pacing-policy.json shareOfAccount gives this company its share. Routines use Haiku or Sonnet only; Opus and Fable never run routines. A Claude seat still takes the smallest tier that does the job.

openrouter.note: The free-model fallback (docs/FREE-MODELS.md): the virtual chain entry openrouter/free resolves to the best free OpenRouter model at each failover tick (company/state/free-models.json, kept by company/tools/free-models.js). Free models may keep or train on what they are sent; every request to them is scrubbed of secrets first and carries a zero max price, so a call can never be billed. Only ids ending :free or listed at price 0 are used; a paid OpenRouter model needs its own id on this list. Remove "free" here (or set freeFallback.enabled false) to turn the fallback off.

candidateDefault._doc: The model a hiring candidate is interviewed on when hire.js is given none (the hire keeps the interviewed model). Must be on the allowed lists above.

routable._doc: Which models scoped routing (docs/ROUTING.md "Scoped routing") may pick by itself: "<provider/model>" or "<provider/prefix>*" -> true|false (the longest key wins; a model with no key is routable, except a needsCeoApproval model, which is off until the owner turns it on). Only the router reads it: a model can still be assigned on purpose (models.js set/chain, hire.js). Owner only: models.js routable <pair> on|off --by owner, or Settings > Models > Automatic picks.

_needsCeoApproval: Model ids a hire or model change may move someone to only with the CEO named in hire.js --approved (the heavy and top Claude tiers).

routing._doc: Which model each routine runs on. Every routine names a scope: an ordered chain of one to three model families (claude, minimax, deepseek). company/tools/pacer.js runs it on the FIRST link of that chain that is open right now, and moves it down the chain when a link closes (Claude or MiniMax over today's pacing line or out of its window, DeepSeek out of credit or near the station rail, a provider that refused the routine). Moving off a closed link happens at once; moving back up waits for the hourly limit and the ramp (pacing-policy.json routing). 'claude' in a chain means the routine's Claude tier (its 'claude' key: haiku or sonnet, never opus or fable). 'minimax' true = MiniMax may run this routine (model-drift.js reads it); set it false for a routine whose chain has no MiniMax link. railOverflow false = the DeepSeek link is still used near the station rail. A routine is matched by exact name or name prefix; one not listed is never touched. Every model here must be on the allowed lists above. The people seat keeps the scopes and who is in each; the CEO approves changes; the pacing numbers are the finance seat's.

scopes._doc: Ordered chains (links: claude, minimax, deepseek; one to three). These are starting defaults: Claude and MiniMax are flat-rate subscriptions, every DeepSeek call costs money, so flat-rate links come first unless the work needs DeepSeek's lane. Code and screens stay off MiniMax by default. The people seat keeps this table, puts each new hire's routine under a scope (routines above) and records who is in each scope in 'who' by seat or function; the CEO approves changes.

ceo.why: the CEO must not go dark: claudeReserve keeps Claude past the daily line (up to the week's hard stop); its writing may fall to MiniMax, then DeepSeek, never to nothing

writing.why: documents and digests, no code; flat-rate Claude, then flat-rate MiniMax

review.why: judgement (security, finance, hiring) on Claude; DeepSeek where Claude's limits bite

code.why: code is written by Claude by default, DeepSeek as the fallback; no MiniMax

actions.why: tool-heavy action work (operations, deploys, devices) where DeepSeek has fewer limits; it also writes code, so no MiniMax

design.why: Claude leads on UI/UX; screens are code, so no MiniMax

research.why: research reads and summarises; flat-rate first, DeepSeek last because it costs per call

seats._doc: Per-seat model chains, kept by company/tools/models.js (and the console: Crew > seat > Model). seats.<station agent id>.chain is an ordered list of {provider, model, effort?}: the first entry is the seat's primary, the rest are its fallbacks. The seat (its roster model and every routine of it) runs on the first entry that can run now and moves back up when a better one recovers (failover below). A seat with a chain is not routed by the pacer's routing table. A new hire starts with [interviewed model, candidateDefault, a connected subscription model, openrouter/free] (the last only while freeFallback is on). Every model must be on the allowed lists above. The owner changes a chain directly; anyone else needs --approved and the self-governance level for models. Optional per seat: claudeReserve (true = its Claude entry ignores the daily pacing line up to the weekly stop; the CEO seat defaults to true; scoped routing never moves such a seat); autoPick (false = the owner pinned this seat's models: scoped routing never moves it, docs/ROUTING.md §8).

failover._doc: How models.js moves a seat along its chain. mode live|shadow (shadow logs what it would do). An entry cannot run when its provider is not connected on the station, the pacer has its subscription closed, a metered provider is near the station's daily rail or out of credit, or the seat's last errorsInARow runs on it were provider errors or a budget hold (held errorHoldMin, then retried). Moving down is immediate; moving back up waits recoverAfterMin of the better entry being able to run, and at most one move up per upAtMostEveryMin. StarNet's station-wide fallback chain (GET/POST /api/fallback/chain) stays the last backstop for a run that fails mid-run.

freeFallback._doc: The free-model fallback (docs/FREE-MODELS.md), used only as the LAST entry of a seat chain, behind its subscriptions: models.js resolves openrouter/free to one real free model when the entries above it cannot run. enabled: shipped false, and a framework update never switches it on; set it true only after the station runs StarNet patch 0022 (setup-station.sh, then a station restart), since before that restart nothing scrubs a request or caps its price. false turns it off everywhere. maxAgeHours: a free-model list older than this is not used. refreshHours: how often the dispatcher re-reads the list. coolMin: a free model whose last run had a provider error is skipped for this long (the next one is used). minItems: graded items a free model needs in the house ranking before its score orders the pick. maxAlternates: how many further free models (0 to 2) the station may fail over to within one request; models.js writes them, picked in the same order, to company/state/free-pick.json, and setup-station.sh passes this cap to the station. A seat may set seats.<id>.class to pick by that task class.
freeFallback._dailyRequests: free-model requests the OpenRouter account may make a day (50 on a free account, more once credits were bought). Scoped routing counts a free model's share of this limit like a subscription's window share (docs/ROUTING.md); it never gates (OpenRouter's own daily-limit error still does).
